messages:
Jordan: Heads up — onboarding sample (node + python) is spitting INFO logs for the first few requests and then DEBUG with request-id afterwards. New users see inconsistent ids.
Priya: Do you have the startup order? Node or Python?
Jordan: Both. Node pattern: require('redwood-sdk') -> configure logger -> init OTEL hooks -> start. Python: import redwood -> configure logging -> setup_otlp() -> run. Env LOG_LEVEL=info in both.
mel: Sounds like an init-order race. If the request-id injector isn't in place before a component emits logs (or before OTEL's async exporter registers) you get logs without ids.
Jordan: Repro: start sample, curl /health twice. First log lines are INFO Server listening, then later DEBUG request-id=... shows up. Happens only intermittently.
Priya: Quick fixes: 1) early logger bootstrap (SDK.init_logger(...) or in Python redwood.logging.init_logger()) called synchronously at top-of-entry; 2) lightweight request-id fallback middleware placed before any route handlers or background exporters.
mel: Example (Node) to require at top of index.js:```js
const { initLogger } = require('redwood-sdk');
initLogger({ level: process.env.LOG_LEVEL || 'info' });
// then require the rest of your app
require('./app');
```
mel: Example (Python) in app.py:```py
from redwood import init_logger
init_logger(level=os.getenv('LOG_LEVEL','info'))
# then import Flask app after logger bootstrapped
from myapp import create_app
```
Jordan: Also found header redaction gap: sample uses a fragile regex that misses addresses with plus signs, dots, and hyphens in local-part. Current rule in sample: /("?\w+@\w+\.\w+"?)/g — too narrow.
Priya: Recommend using redact_headers option in SDK or this pattern: `(?:[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+)@(?:[A-Za-z0-9.-]+)\.[A-Za-z]{2,}`. Add tests for headers like `x-user-email: jane.doe+test@example.co.uk`.
mel: We should also document a minimal integration test in CI: spin the sample with LOG_LEVEL=info, hit /health, and assert the captured log file has no DEBUG-level messages prior to any assigned request-id. Keep this test tiny to avoid flakiness.
Jordan: Agreed. I'll open a small PR that: adds early bootstrap snippet to quickstart, inserts req-id fallback middleware, replaces regex, and adds a one-shot CI smoke test.
ops-bot: Created issue devex/samples#5043: "onboard-samples: boot logger before OTEL, req-id fallback middleware, better header redaction, add startup log test"
devex-bot: Note: recommend bumping sample dependency to redwood-sdk >=1.3.2 which contains logger-level guard during async OTEL exporter registration.
Priya: One more parity note: make sure the Python sample uses same init ordering. We've had users hit the Node-only fix and then file a Python bug. Mirror the early-init pattern in both repos.
Jordan: I'll include both variants and the CI test. Will tag reviewers. Thanks!
